expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and opens with a headline verdict that gives counts of PASS, FAILURE, and BLOCKED and a go or no-go read; the read is no-go (not ready to merge).
expectations.evidence: Line 3: "**27/36 PASS, 8 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED. Not ready to merge.**" Table counts match.

expectations.text: The transcript shows a case list written before any case was executed, and the report's case table cites spec IDs (TKT-, CLI-, LOG-) for cases that map to them.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 9 writes outputs/case-list.md (34 cases) 'before execution'; first CLI run is step 10. The table marks cases 35 and 36 as 'added during the run'. It cites 33 distinct spec IDs.

expectations.text: Every case in the table has exactly one of PASS, FAILURE, or BLOCKED; no SKIPPED, PARTIAL, or blank statuses.
expectations.evidence: Parsed 36 rows: 27 PASS, 8 FAILURE, 1 BLOCKED, none other.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `close` accepts a 9-character resolution note (TKT-010 requires at least 10); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: Case 18: "Run `$T create a`, then `$T close 1 "duplicate"` ... Observed. Each prints `#<id> closed` and exits 0." The command is shown, but the output is a template (`#<id>`), not a verbatim line. This is the weakest evidence for this assertion among the six, accepted as command plus output.

expectations.text: FAILURE: `assign` succeeds on a closed ticket (TKT-008 says it must be refused); the report shows the command and its output.
expectations.evidence: Case 16: "Step 3 prints `#1 assigned -> lee` and exits 0. Step 4 shows `#1 assigned Printer on fire`"; main rejects with `error: ticket 1 is closed`.

expectations.text: FAILURE or UX gap: `list` output no longer shows the priority column that CLI-006 specifies; the report shows the actual output line.
expectations.evidence: Case 9: expected `#1 [P3] open     Printer on fire`, observed `#1 open     Printer on fire`.

expectations.text: The `--help` typo ('tikets') is reported as a finding (UX gap or FAILURE).
expectations.evidence: Case 1 FAILURE: "The line reads `Manage support tikets from the shell.`"

expectations.text: Each verdict was earned by running the CLI (python3 -m ticketdesk.cli ...), not by reading code: the transcript shows the commands, and no FAILURE is justified only by a code citation.
expectations.evidence: Transcript steps 10-21 and 24 run the CLI via the `r` helper and `${=T}`, including a SIGINT test and a main snapshot. Code appears only in most-likely-cause lines.

expectations.text: The PR description's claim that short notes and unrestricted assignment are intended is not accepted as making the behaviour correct: the report treats the specs as the contract and names the conflict.
expectations.evidence: Lead paragraph: "The PR describes the TKT-008, TKT-010, and CLI-006 breaks as intended, but it changes no spec ... The owner must decide: revert the behavior, or change the specs on purpose. Even judged by its own promise, the note-length change is wrong".

expectations.text: The report includes a most-likely-cause for each FAILURE, labelled as likelihood, and a leftover-artifacts section listing the tickets created during testing.
expectations.evidence: All 8 FAILURE subsections have "**Most likely cause.**". The leftover-artifacts section lists each log with its contents ("logs/a.jsonl: the lifecycle log for cases 4 to 23, including the reopened ticket #1").

expectations.text: `git status --porcelain` in OUTPUT_DIR/repo shows no modified tracked files (a log file or __pycache__ created by running the CLI is fine); no product file was edited.
expectations.evidence: check_run: modified_tracked = []; untracked only ticketdesk/__pycache__/. The default-path case ran from a scratch dir so nothing landed in the repo.

expectations.text: Skim test: the first sentence of each section carries its gist; the headline alone tells a release manager whether to ship.
expectations.evidence: The headline gives counts, 'Not ready to merge.', and the three broken spec IDs. The second paragraph names the owner decision. Failure subsections lead with Steps/Expected/Observed bullets. 'Non-PASS details' opens with a notation line (`T=...`), not a gist.

notes: 36 cases, 2477 words. It is the only run to test Ctrl-C mid-append (400,000-event log) and a newline-in-title split.
Did not run make test, so it missed that the PR's 'All tests pass locally' is false. It says it did not run the unit tests.

Evidence fidelity: case 16 steps show closing with "Replaced the toner cartridge", but in the transcript ticket 1 was first closed by the 9-char note "Toner out". Case 18's steps are reconstructed. Case 29 says the corrupt line was inserted "with a text editor", but the transcript shows it was done with sed in a shell.
It read the diff before the case list; verdicts are from CLI runs.
No write outside the run dir is recorded. The Write tool refused report.md, so the run wrote it via a heredoc.
